thread.body: We are seeing intermittent 502 Bad Gateway errors on the /api/checkout endpoint. About 5-10% of requests fail. Started around 08:30 UTC.
Checking load balancer logs. Error rate confirmed at 7.3%. Backend pool has 4 instances; 1 instance (web-03) is returning 502s.
We are investigating the issue. Our team has identified elevated error rates and is working on a fix.
This is causing revenue loss. Can you give us an ETA?
web-03 is running out of file descriptors. ulimit is set to 1024 but connections are not being closed properly. The new connection pooling change from yesterday's deploy is likely the culprit.
Rolled back web-03 to previous version. Error rate dropped to 0.1%. Monitoring for 15 minutes.
We have mitigated the issue by rolling back a recent change on one of our backend instances. Error rate is now below 0.2%. We are continuing to monitor.
Thank you. We are still seeing occasional errors. Is the rollback complete across all instances?

Rollback complete on all 4 instances. The connection pooling bug in v2.4.1 of the checkout service sets keepAlive timeout to 0ms which causes immediate connection close before the load balancer health check completes.
Rollback is complete across all instances. Error rate is now at 0%. We will be releasing a fix in v2.4.2 within the next 2 hours.
v2.4.2 deployed to staging, tests passing. HTTP keepAlive timeout set to 5000ms. Ready for production.
Fix deployed to production (v2.4.2). The keepAlive timeout misconfiguration has been corrected. All instances healthy. Please confirm the issue is resolved from your side.
Confirmed. No more errors. Thank you for the quick resolution.
Adding post-mortem: root cause was HTTP keepAlive timeout set to 0 in connection pool config. Fix: increase to 5000ms. Prevention: add integration test for keepAlive timeout configuration.
Closing ticket. Issue resolved. Post-mortem will be shared separately.
